title: Makoda Turns Claude and ChatGPT Plans Into Free Local API
summary: Makoda launches as free Mac and Ubuntu app that converts existing ChatGPT and Claude subscriptions into local and remote APIs, eliminating per-token bills.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Makoda launches as a free Mac and Ubuntu app that transforms existing ChatGPT and Claude subscriptions into functioning local and remote APIs.
- Developers can eliminate separate API bills by reusing compute from consumer plans they already pay for during application testing phases.
- The tool addresses a billing gap where testing AI integrations often costs $100-plus monthly on top of existing consumer subscriptions.


Developers testing AI-integrated applications now have a way to avoid double-paying for compute. Makoda, a free desktop application for Mac and Ubuntu, officially launched on November 6, 2026, converting existing ChatGPT (Codex) and Claude consumer subscriptions into functioning local and remote APIs. The tool targets the billing friction developers face when they pay for consumer AI plans but still need separate, per-token API access for application testing.


## The Double-Billing Problem


Many developers maintain ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro subscriptions for daily work while simultaneously paying for API access to test applications. This dual-subscription model can add $100 to $150 in monthly costs purely for development environments. Makoda's creator reported spending approximately $120 per month in API bills on top of existing consumer plans, a common pain point for solo developers and small teams building AI-powered products.


The application runs locally on developer machines, intercepting requests that would normally route to paid API endpoints. By reusing compute already allocated through consumer subscriptions, Makoda eliminates the need for separate API billing during development and testing phases.


## Release Date and Availability


Makoda officially released on November 6, 2026, with immediate availability for Mac and Ubuntu operating systems. The application is distributed as a free download, with no usage caps or per-request charges. Developers can access both local API endpoints for on-machine testing and remote endpoints for distributed development scenarios.


## How the Bridge Works


Makoda functions as middleware between developer applications and AI model interfaces. The software authenticates using existing ChatGPT or Claude session credentials, then exposes standard API endpoints that mirror commercial API response formats. Applications built to consume OpenAI or Anthropic APIs can point to Makoda endpoints without code changes, routing requests through consumer-plan compute instead of metered API infrastructure.


Key technical features include:


- Drop-in replacement for standard API endpoints with compatible response formatting
- Local execution for privacy-sensitive testing workflows
- Remote endpoint generation for team collaboration scenarios
- Support for both streaming and batch request patterns


## Target Use Cases


The tool addresses specific development workflows where API costs accumulate rapidly. Prototyping phases, where developers iterate on prompts and integration logic, generate high request volumes without production value. Makoda shifts these testing costs to existing subscription allocations, preserving API budgets for production deployment.


Solo developers building side projects benefit most directly, as they often lack separate development infrastructure budgets. Small teams testing multiple integration approaches can also reduce overhead by consolidating compute costs into existing team subscriptions rather than provisioning separate API keys.


## What This Means


Makoda's launch highlights a structural inefficiency in AI development workflows. As consumer AI subscriptions and developer API access diverge in pricing models, tools that bridge the gap become economically necessary. For developers already subscribed to ChatGPT or Claude for productivity, Makoda converts sunk costs into development resources. The approach may pressure API providers to offer integrated development tiers or reconsider how consumer and developer access models align, particularly as application testing becomes a standard phase in AI-augmented software development.
